answer: An escalating identity bond resists Sybils: the first identity is nearly free, but each additional identity from the same operator requires a much larger refundable deposit, so fielding a thousand sockpuppets means climbing a canyon wall of locked capital while an honest user pays almost nothing. The maths is stark — fake volume only profits while the bond stays below the scam's gain — and operators who strike in the sable hours before dawn face the same wall, since every fresh identity must post its bond before it can trade.
